newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends up 1.28 pct on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends up 1.28 pct on foreign buying.

text.p: The Jakarta stock market touched a high for the year of 634.41 points on Thursday before easing back to 634.30 at the close, powered by overseas interest in banking stocks and selected blue-chips, brokers said.
A broker for a London-based securities firm said a central bank cut in its key discount rate for short-term paper boosted market sentiment.
"I expect the market will continue to rally at least for a couple of days unless there is major negative news," he said.
The Jakarta Composite Index ended up 8.03 points, or 1.28 percent, at 634.30 points.
Advancers led decliners by 62 to 41, with 64 counters unchanged. Total volume was 220.6 million shares with a value of 507.3 billion rupiah.
Brokers anticipated U.S. and British investors would enter the market on Friday and help the index up further.

Bank Indonesia cut its key discount rate for short-term paper (SBPUs) by 50 basis points for all maturities, bringing the one-week SBPU to 15.25 percent, two to 15.50 percent, and one-, three-, six- and 12-month to 16.0 percent.
"It is a sign of a cooling economy and it's good for the stock exchange. Banking stocks have benefited a lot because funding costs are getting lower," a foreign broker said.
Bank Negara Indonesia, BDNI, Bank International Indonesia and Bank Danamon were active targets for fresh buying, brokers said.
Bank Negara Indonesia topped the active list with 71.4 million shares traded. It rose 100 rupiah to 1,375 rupiah, while Bank International Indonesia rose 50 rupiah to 2,525 on 10.1 million shares.
More blue-chips joined the active list during the afternoon session on fresh overseas buying which gave a further boost to market sentiment, brokers said.
Blue-chip toll operator Citra Marga and secondaries marble producer Citatah and transportation firm Steady Safe were actively sought, brokers said.
Citra Marga rose 50 rupiah to 2,000 on a volume of 8.7 million shares, while Citatah rose 100 rupiah to 1,700 on about 2.6 million shares.
Brokers said there was also continued buying interest in heavyweights telecommunication firm Telkom, cement maker Semen Gresik and cigarette firm Sampoerna.
